scope: Follow-up Standard scheduler audit and local runtime replacement; private operational evidence. Source hashes identify the uncommitted working-tree artifact.
auditFindings: Engine wall-clock last use and a local selection counter could distort live fairness; checkpoint data now seeds first use only.
Stale reservation callbacks could release a newer selection; releases now require their ownership token.
Multiple cooled accounts could begin recovery together; new recovery selections now share a monotonic five-second interval while healthy work continues.
Repeated quota frames could multiply backoff within one job; escalation now counts the job once while fresh notices retain or extend its deadline.
Expired reset-less zero observations could reopen cooldown before a permitted probe; the old observations retire at probe admission and new observations still exclude.
Synchronous grant cleanup could erase the success signal before recovery reset; confirmed recovery now survives cleanup and is checkpointed.
A delayed lookup could dispatch abandoned work or rely on old readiness; both caller presence and projection freshness are checked before new selection.

localAcceptance.scope: local VM separation on one trusted Mac; no provider generation or cloud deployment

installation.workflow: Built final source under recovery-20260915, inspected and loaded only into Standard VM; updated reviewed manifest and reinstalled component overlay; confirmed Standard empty/execution-closed via scoped viewer; stopped only Standard runtime; normal up respected the central ownership wait; inspected running image and preserved volume; passed local acceptance.

rollback: Restore preceding rotation-20260915 Standard pin with execution closed, preserve state and ownership fence, and requalify. The preceding image lacks this follow-up recovery/fairness protection; rollback does not clear quotas or authorize unknown work.
limits: No real provider sign-in, quota spend, generation, throughput measurement or public application deployment. Local empty-pool acceptance does not establish provider readiness.
Five seconds bounds new local recovery selections, not a provider quota. Long recovery jobs on different accounts can overlap if their selections are spaced by the interval.
The recovery budget, live rotation and central-denial history are process-local. Restart starts a new local budget; central ownership/grants and persisted provider cooldowns remain authoritative.
Checkpoint writes are best effort. Successful filesystem persistence is not an execution grant; no PostgreSQL schema, role, RLS policy or central budget change was made.
Request fairness does not imply equal token consumption. A sole healthy eligible account can receive consecutive completed jobs.
Monitor health remains centrally observed metadata, not live scheduler capacity. No browser UI or operator telemetry feed was added.
Cancellation avoidance applies before forwarding. Once forwarded, uncertain work retains its original key/account/epoch and cannot be repeated or moved.
Only Standard runtime was replaced. Premium, central and monitor image IDs retain their preceding pins. The trusted Mac remains the common physical host.
